projectContext.name: Outpatient Appointment System
projectContext.description: When users submit appointment requests, the API intermittently returns HTTP 500 (e.g., third-party calendar service timeouts or malformed responses). Exceptions bubble up directly. In some cases the appointment is written to the local DB but calendar sync fails; the frontend only sees failure, and repeated submissions can reserve multiple slots.
projectContext.currentVersion: Lacks idempotency, compensation, and unified state management for calendar sync exceptions; errors are not standardized.
projectContext.targetVersion: Reliable_Appointment_Booking_v2 (more resilient to runtime/API failures, clear states, and idempotent retries)

issueStatement: Appointment confirmations crash (HTTP 500) due to external calendar sync exceptions/timeouts. Exceptions are uncaught; without compensation or idempotency, retries may double-book a slot. Users may see failure while the slot is actually reserved, causing inconsistent state.
businessGoals: Eliminate false negatives/positives: on failure responses, guarantee no slot is reserved; if reserved, return success or mark "in-progress" and confirm later.
Introduce idempotent handling keyed by a unique client request ID to prevent double booking.
Standardize error codes and emit structured logs to speed troubleshooting and reconciliation.

stack: Calendar sync via HTTP/gRPC can timeout or return invalid data.
Use a simulated calendar service for analysis/fixes; do not call the real third-party.

nonFunctional: Design 5 integration test scenarios: normal success; calendar timeout -> 500 with no booking; idempotent retry without double booking; partial success triggers compensation; audit verification. Runnable via a single script.
Emit structured logs at each stage with a unique appointment/request ID (redacted sensitive data) for reconciliation.
